# Results — Study 824 (Cochrane-Piazzesi Factor)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Cochrane &
Piazzesi (2005), *"Bond Risk Premia"*: a **single** tent-shaped linear combination of forward
rates forecasts the one-year-ahead **excess return** of Treasury bonds across every maturity,
with an R² a plain curve slope cannot match. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar
month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `03a5e9844a31` (cached tape).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **2002-01-02 → 2026-06-30**, 6,162 rows |
| Yields | `^IRX` (13w ≈ 0.25y), `^FVX` (5y), `^TNX` (10y), `^TYX` (30y) constant-maturity indices (annualised %), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Bonds | `SHY` (1-3y), `IEF` (7-10y), `TLT` (20y+) total-return ETF prices |
| Forwards | each yield treated as a continuously-compounded zero (`p(n) = −n·y(n)`); implied forwards `f(n1→n2) = (n2·y2 − n1·y1)/(n2 − n1)` → the vector `[y_short, f(0.25→5), f(5→10), f(10→30)]`, public at the close of `t` |
| LHS | each ETF's realised **252-day total return** minus the one-year risk-free (`^IRX` bill yield at `t`); averaged across the three ETFs → `avg_rx_{t→t+252}` (n = **5,760** overlapping obs) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → duration position held day `t`. The timer charges one-way cost × traded NAV per switch |
| Statistics | HAC (Newey-West, **378-lag** ≈ 1.5× the 252-day overlap) predictive regression; a Campbell-Thompson out-of-sample R²; a 1,000-draw block-rotation placebo; a two-era cut; a costed duration timer; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Signal caveat — named on the Signal axis.** Cochrane & Piazzesi used the Fama-Bliss clean
1-…-5-year zero-coupon file; the retail stack only exposes the coarse 0.25 / 5 / 10 / 30-year
constant-maturity grid, so this is a **four-forward proxy** of their five-forward factor. The
grid is coarse and the magnitudes approximate — but the honesty rails below do not depend on the
grid being fine.

## The headline — the predictive regression / CP factor

Regress `avg_rx_{t+252}` on `[1, y_short, f_1, f_2, f_3]`; the fitted value is the CP factor.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| in-sample predictive **R²** | **0.226** |
| single-factor predictive slope (`avg_rx = a + b·CP`) | 1.000 |
| Newey-West(378) *t* on that slope | **+2.62** |
| average 1y excess return (LHS mean) | +166.7 bps |

The loadings trace the **right tent**: `y_short −0.06`, `f_1 −2.11`, **`f_2 +4.92`** (the peak, on
the 5→10y forward), `f_3 −0.97` — negative-short, positive-middle, negative-long, exactly the
Cochrane-Piazzesi shape. *Individually* every forward's HAC *t* is insignificant (|t| ≤ 1.1); the
factor is a joint object.

**But the naive HAC *t* is not evidence here.** The regressors are near-unit-root persistent and
the 252-day returns overlap, so the single-factor HAC *t* is badly **size-distorted**: on a 20-seed
**null** synthetic world (below) this exact statistic averages **+2.08** and fires |t| ≥ 2 on
**11/20** nulls. The observed +2.62 sits barely half a standard deviation above what pure
persistence manufactures. The honest bar is the out-of-sample R² and the placebo.

## Out-of-sample — does it beat the prevailing mean?

Expanding-window Campbell-Thompson R² of the CP forecast vs the naive prevailing-mean forecast
(227 non-overlapping forecasts):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **out-of-sample R²** | **−0.27** |

The CP forecast is **worse than a constant** out of sample — negative OOS R². The 0.226 in-sample
fit does not survive into a real forecast.

## Placebo — is the in-sample R² a lucky alignment?

Block-rotate the forward-return target against the forward matrix (block = 252, preserving the
overlap autocorrelation), 1,000 rotations:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed R² | 0.226 |
| placebo mean R² (sd) | **0.180** (0.054) |
| right-tail p | **0.208** |

A persistent-regressor null **already manufactures R² ≈ 0.18 with no true link**; the observed
0.226 is only ~0.9σ above it (p = 0.21, not significant). This is the Bauer-Hamilton (2018)
spurious-regression point in one table: on persistent yields a large predictive R² is close to
free.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2014-01-01)

| era | n | R² | single-factor NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2002-01 → 2014-01 | 2,620 | 0.412 | **+3.90** |
| 2014-01 → 2026-06 | 2,888 | 0.114 | +1.72 |

Whatever in-sample fit exists is **concentrated in the first half** (the QE / falling-rate era) and
fades to insignificance afterwards — not a stable forecaster.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Own TLT (duration) when the *out-of-sample* CP forecast is above its expanding-median, else cash;
one-way cost × traded NAV per switch, signal known at `t−1`, held `t`.

| one-way cost | net Sharpe | buy-and-hold TLT Sharpe | switches/yr | invested |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **2 bps** | **+0.02** | +0.22 | 3.7 | 47% |
| **5 bps** | **+0.005** | +0.22 | 3.7 | 47% |

The CP-timed duration book earns a Sharpe of essentially **zero** and sits far below simply holding
TLT — the signal *subtracts* value. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded tape whose realised one-year excess return equals a controlled target
*exactly* (interleaved residue-class construction). Under `edge = 0` the target is white; under
`edge > 0` it loads on a tent-shaped forward contrast.

| world | in-sample R² | OOS R² | naive single-factor NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **0.0007** (max 0.0019) | +0.019 | mean +2.08, fires **11/20** |
| planted (`edge = 0.05`, seed 824) | **0.661** | **+0.631** | +100 |

The **R²** and the **OOS R²** are the trustworthy detectors: silent on the null (≈ 0), lit on the
planted edge (0.66 / +0.63). The raw single-factor HAC *t* is **not** — it fires on 11/20 nulls,
confirming why the real-tape stamp rests on the OOS R² and placebo, never the raw *t*. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** On the coarse constant-maturity grid the Cochrane-Piazzesi regression does
  produce an in-sample R² of **0.226** with correctly **tent-shaped** loadings (peak on the 5→10y
  forward) and a strong first era (*t* = +3.90) — the claim's fingerprint is visibly present. But
  it is **not a robust edge**: a block placebo puts that R² at **p = 0.21** (persistent regressors
  alone deliver R² ≈ 0.18), the **out-of-sample R² is −0.27** (worse than a constant), the second
  era is insignificant (*t* = +1.72), and the headline HAC *t* = +2.62 sits inside the synthetic
  null's own distribution of that size-distorted statistic (mean +2.08). Right shape, no robust
  forecasting power — a Weak/Fragile in-sample pattern, exactly the Bauer-Hamilton spurious-
  regression reading of the CP factor on a persistent yield curve.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The CP-timed duration book earns a net Sharpe of ~**0.02** (2 bps) /
  **0.005** (5 bps) versus **0.22** for simply holding TLT — the signal subtracts value even before
  a serious cost. No paycheck.
